messages:
customer_engr: Hey team — after we cut over Prod to the PrivateLink endpoint for redwood-private-api, about 60% of requests are failing with TLS handshake errors (app sees 502/connection reset). No change on client side. :confused:
support_lynn: Thanks — can you share curl -v output and what DNS returns from the client side? Also any NAT/proxy in front of the endpoint?
customer_engr: curl -v:

  $ curl -v https://api.redwood-private.internal/v1/ping
  *   Trying 10.10.200.45...
  * Connected to api.redwood-private.internal (10.10.200.45) port 443 (#0)
  * TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
  * TLS: handshake failure
  * Closing connection 0
  curl: (35) TLS handshake failure

customer_engr: dig +short api.redwood-private.internal -> 10.10.200.45 (this is the vpce eni IP in our subnet). We do go through an internal proxy EC2 (haproxy) in the same subnet for logging/acl.
sre_nina: Can you run tcpdump on the proxy and on the client when reproducing? We want to see the TLS ClientHello and which side sends RST. A quick traceroute might help too.
customer_engr: tcpdump (client -> proxy -> VPCE):

  client 10.0.5.12 > 10.10.200.45: TLS ClientHello
  10.10.200.45 > 10.0.5.12: RST, ack 1  <-- RST comes from the VPCE ENI

  proxy shows ClientHello forwarded, then RST appears to originate from 10.10.200.45, not from our proxy.

support_lynn: Interesting. Two quick checks: 1) is source/dest check enabled on the proxy EC2? 2) Security group on the VPCE allowing ephemeral ports back to the client? Many vpce SGs only allow 443 from customer CIDR and forget ephemeral high ports.
infra_jordan: Also confirm whether the proxy is doing SNAT. If the proxy forwards without SNAT, the endpoint will reply to the original client IP; if routing is asymmetric, replies can be dropped.
customer_engr: Our proxy had source/dest check ON (we forgot the change after migrating). Proxy does NOT SNAT (we rely on routing). SG on the vpce is restrictive: inbound 443 from proxy IP only, outbound 1024-65535 limited to 10.0.0.0/16 (we had a narrow ephemeral range).
sre_nina: That aligns: if proxy forwards traffic without SNAT but the route table sends return traffic directly to the VPC endpoint or TGW, packets can be sent back to client IPs that the proxy doesn't own and get dropped by rp_filter or by the proxy's ENI source/dest. Also vpce SG needs to allow ephemeral source ports so TLS handshake can complete.
support_lynn: Repro steps we recommend: (1) disable source/dest check on the proxy ENI OR enable SNAT on proxy so return traffic flows through it, (2) temporarily widen VPCE SG outbound to 1024-65535 to client CIDR, (3) run curl again and capture tcpdump.
customer_engr: Did the quick change: disabled source/dest check on haproxy instance and expanded vpce SG outbound ephemeral range. Re-tested and TLS is now successful. curl -v shows completed handshake and 200 OK. :tada:

  $ curl -v https://api.redwood-private.internal/v1/ping
  * Connected to api.redwood-private.internal (10.10.200.45) port 443 (#0)
  * TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
  > GET /v1/ping HTTP/1.1
  < HTTP/1.1 200 OK

customer_engr: Root cause summary we found: proxy EC2 had source/dest check enabled and we were forwarding without SNAT, causing asymmetric routing for return packets; VPCE security group also blocked ephemeral port range, which prevented proper TLS client/server port negotiation.
sre_nina: Great catch — adding notes to runbook: when placing inline proxies before a VPCE, either ensure proxy performs SNAT or disable source/dest check and adjust route table so reply path returns correctly; make sure vpce SGs include ephemeral port ranges for customer CIDRs.
deploy-bot: Incident doc created: https://go.redwood/internal/incidents/2055554321-vpce-proxy-routing-tls
support_lynn: Thanks for the quick turnaround. Will follow up with a recommended config snippet for customers.

RECOMMENDED CONFIG SNIPPET:

  - If using EC2 proxy in-path: either 
      * Enable SNAT on proxy (iptables MASQUERADE) so downstream sees proxy IP, OR
      * Disable source/dest check on proxy ENI and ensure route table sends replies back to proxy (not direct to TGW/ENI).
  - VPCE security group: allow ephemeral ranges outbound and inbound as needed (1024-65535) between VPCE and customer CIDRs for TCP sessions.
  - Test steps: dig to VPCE eni IP, curl -v, tcpdump on both sides, check for RST origin.
